caption:
Apple is testing daily limits on advanced Siri AI requests in its 27.3 betas.
Everyday tasks like timers and messages keep working, but heavier requests can pause until the limit resets around midnight.
iCloud+ plans from 200GB up raise the allowance, up to 20 times on the 12TB plan.

Would you pay more for iCloud to keep Siri AI going?

paragraphs.text: Apple is testing daily usage limits for advanced Siri AI requests in the iOS 27.3, iPadOS 27.3 and macOS 27.3 betas, with higher allowances available to iCloud+ subscribers, according to iPhone in Canada and Business Upturn. Both outlets cite an Apple support document published on November 16, 2026, and reporting by MacRumors.

Each device receives a free daily allowance for several categories of work, according to the support document as described by iPhone in Canada. The categories are advanced Siri requests, image generation and editing, Shortcuts that run on Apple's cloud models, and third-party apps that use those models through Private Cloud Compute.

Business Upturn lists the features in more detail: Image Playground, the Clean Up, Extend and Spatial Reframing photo tools, Shortcuts that use the AFM Cloud or Cloud Pro models, and apps built on Apple Foundation Models.

Routine requests are not affected. Setting a timer, setting an alarm or sending a simple message keeps working after the allowance runs out, both outlets report. Requests that draw on personal context can pause until the allowance resets or the user moves to a larger plan.

The 50GB iCloud+ plan keeps the standard allowance. The 200GB plan raises it to up to two times the standard, the 2TB plan to up to five times, the 6TB plan to up to ten times and the 12TB plan to up to 20 times. Access to the Cloud Pro model in Shortcuts also starts at the 200GB tier.

The extra capacity is shared across the devices on one Apple Account and with members of a Family Sharing group, in the order it is used. Existing subscribers receive the higher limits without a price increase, according to iPhone in Canada.

Apple has not published a fixed number of requests. The company says limits depend on the complexity of a task and on demand. Allowances generally reset around midnight, and unused requests do not carry over to the next day.

The higher Siri AI access through iCloud+ is not offered in Brazil, the European Union, the United Kingdom or South Korea, Business Upturn reports. The wider Apple Intelligence increase also excludes China.

The test turns iCloud+, until now a storage subscription, into the way Apple meters its most expensive AI features. Other AI providers already cap heavy use on free tiers, and Apple is applying a similar model while keeping basic Siri tasks outside the meter. Because the free allowance has no published number, users will only learn where the line sits by reaching it.
The limits appear only in beta software so far. The signal to watch is whether they remain in the public 27.3 release and whether Apple publishes concrete request numbers for the free allowance.
